competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can grasp what a speaker implies without ever stating it.
Can understand extended speech in which the relationship between points is only implied and not signalled explicitly.

competencies.displayName: Detect the position an account takes
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can discern the position an account is written from without it being declared.
Can notice when a question has been answered around rather than answered.
Can work out why a speaker is raising a matter at that particular moment.
Can sense a reservation the other person has not put into words and bring it into the open.
Can act on a hint offered in place of a direct request.
Can put a request obliquely enough to leave the other person room to pass it by.
Can draw significance from what the other person declines to say.
Can appreciate distinctions of style between two treatments of the same subject.
Can pitch their wording to the degree of formality an occasion calls for.
Can hold a formal register across a long stretch without lapsing out of it.
Can tell when a wording belongs to an earlier period.
Can tell one regional variety of the language from another.

competencies.displayName: Adapt to the other speaker's register
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can bring their own level of formality into line with the person they are addressing.
Can tell when wording has been cast in the manner of official documents.
Can put what an official text demands into wording anyone would follow.

competencies.displayName: Judge a wording as too strong
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can judge that a phrasing would strike its hearer as harsher than was meant.
Can present a clear, detailed description of a complex subject integrating its sub-themes.
Can develop a particular point at length within a longer contribution.
Can bring an extended contribution to a close with an appropriate conclusion.
Can tell the listener in advance how a long contribution will be laid out.
Can bind a long stretch together with connectors that make its organisation visible.
Can depart from the thread and pick it up again without losing the listener.
Can retain a turn long enough to bring an involved point to completion.
Can dwell on whichever part of a contribution carries the weight.
Can begin on an involved subject in a way that establishes why it warrants attention.
Can relate their own contribution skilfully to those of other speakers.
Can take up another speaker's point and carry it forward as their own contribution.
Can draw into the exchange someone who has not yet spoken.

competencies.displayName: Restore the floor to an interrupted speaker
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can hand the turn back to a speaker who was cut across.
Can bring a wandering exchange back to the matter in hand.
Can point out that two other speakers are agreeing without having realised it.

competencies.displayName: Sum up where a group stands
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can state where a group has arrived and what it has left open.
Can break in on a speaker without breaking their thread.
Can end a group exchange having established what is to happen next.
Can deploy idiomatic expressions with a sure grasp of their force.

competencies.displayName: Follow colloquial speech not aimed at them
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can follow colloquial speech between speakers who are making no allowance for a learner.

competencies.displayName: Judge when an idiom would jar
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can judge when an idiomatic turn would be out of keeping.

competencies.displayName: Use a set phrase in its exact sense
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can employ a fixed expression in precisely the sense it carries.
Can arrive at the sense of unfamiliar slang from the exchange surrounding it.
Can tell when a mild wording is standing in for a blunt one.
Can substitute a softened wording where the direct one would give offence.
Can catch a passing reference to something the culture holds in common.
Can receive a proverbial saying in the sense it was offered.
Can express themselves fluently and spontaneously without much obvious searching for expressions.

competencies.displayName: Select from a broad range of formulations
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can select a formulation from a broad range without having to curtail what they wish to say.
Can keep the turn while working out how to put something.
Can meet an unforeseen change of direction in an exchange with no preparation.

competencies.displayName: Sustain fluency on a formal occasion
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can maintain fluency under the pressure of a formal occasion.
Can speak at length on an involved subject with no time to prepare.

competencies.displayName: Recover from being put on the spot
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can regain composure and carry on after being caught unprepared in front of others.
Can hold to exact wording at ordinary conversational speed.

competencies.displayName: Use language flexibly for professional ends
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can use language flexibly and effectively for social, academic and professional purposes.
Can put a proposal to those with the standing to decide on it.
Can take questions on a proposal and answer them as they come.
Can conduct a meeting through its business to a close.

competencies.displayName: Brief someone on a complex matter
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can bring a colleague abreast of an involved matter quickly.
Can set out the method by which a result was arrived at.
Can uphold a finding against informed questioning.
Can work the terms of an agreement out and state them precisely enough to be relied on.
Can turn down a request from a colleague without harm to the standing between them.
Can put a case on behalf of another person.

competencies.displayName: Represent a position not their own
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can set out fairly a position they do not personally hold.
Can put a case to someone holding authority over the outcome.
Can frame a formal request in the terms the occasion demands.
Can state what someone is owed and on what footing.
Can lodge an objection formally so that it stands on the record.
Can voice the sense of a group they represent in place of their own view.
Can contest a decision through whatever channel is provided for it.
Can give up a claim shown to be unfounded without loss of standing.
Can understand contemporary literary prose.
Can take a metaphor in the sense its author intended.
Can carry a point by figurative comparison rather than by statement.
Can notice the imagery a passage works by and what it is doing there.
Can see what a recurring element in a work is standing for.
Can consider how a writer achieves an effect and not merely what was said.
Can render a figurative passage into plain wording without losing its point.
Can identify the tone a written passage adopts toward its subject.

competencies.displayName: Compare two treatments of a theme
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can set two works handling the same theme against one another.
Can help two people at odds understand what the other is actually claiming.

competencies.displayName: Restate a position for the other side
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can put one side's position in terms the opposing side would accept as fair.
Can locate what two opposed parties already hold in common.
Can bring down the temperature of an exchange that has grown heated.
Can explain to one person why another's conduct carries a different sense in their culture.
Can carry meaning between speakers of the two languages they command.
Can scale what they say to someone with less of the language without condescending to them.
Can establish that a resolution is genuinely accepted by both parties.
Can hold to a neutral footing while bringing two sides toward agreement.
Can assess a piece of work against criteria that were set in advance.
Can say what would make a piece of work better and on what grounds.

competencies.displayName: Appraise a work's strengths and weaknesses
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can appraise where a piece of work succeeds and where it falls down.
Can give a considered review of a work they have encountered.
Can question an assertion made by someone with greater standing in the subject.

competencies.displayName: Assess the reliability of a source
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can judge how much weight an account merits given where it originated.
Can show that a parallel breaks down at the point where it was being relied on.
Can observe that two things occurring together does not establish that one produced the other.
Can commend something while making the limits of the commendation plain.
Can carry two possible readings forward together until one of them is settled.
Can point out that what was said admits more than one reading.
Can establish which of two readings was intended without appearing obtuse.
Can act usefully on information they know to be incomplete.
Can identify what an exchange has failed to settle.

competencies.displayName: Answer a question built on a false premise
competencies.cefrDescriptor: Can answer a question whose premise they reject, rather than simply refusing it.
Can act on an instruction too loose to follow literally, and state what they assumed.
Can keep from committing until the position is clear without appearing to dodge.
Can leave a matter open on purpose and signal that the vagueness is intended.
